title: Ion & gas tests
examples: How do I know if a gas is chlorine or bromine?
What does a yellow flame color tell me about an ion?
Can I use a precipitate test to find out about dissolved ions?

explain.say: Today we learn how to test unknown ions in samples. We use three main methods for this. The first method is the flame test.
When we heat a sample in a flame, certain metal ions give off specific colors. For example, sodium ions give a bright yellow color. Potassium ions produce a lilac or pale purple color.
The second test involves looking for precipitates. A precipitate is a solid that forms when two solutions mix. For instance, mixing silver nitrate and sodium chloride forms a white precipitate.
Our third test is gas testing. This checks for specific gases like chlorine or ammonia. For example, passing gas through acidified potassium permanganate gives a distinct color change.

draw.text: Gas Tests: Color changes indicate gas

explain.say: Imagine you test an unknown salt solution. You first run a flame test and see a yellow color. Then you add a reagent and see a white solid form. Finally, you test the gas produced and it changes color. This helps identify the ion.
A common mistake is assuming all yellow flames are sodium. You must use a flame test kit or check for other ions to be sure. Always test for multiple ions to confirm your results.

items: Do not assume one color means one ion.

faq.q: What is the difference between a precipitate and a colored solution?
faq.a: A precipitate is a solid substance that falls out of a solution. A colored solution means the dissolved ions are making the liquid appear colored.
asks: How do I tell if something is dissolved or solid?

faq.q: Why are flame tests so useful in chemistry?
faq.a: Flame tests are useful because different metal ions emit specific, unique colors when heated. This allows us to identify what metals are present.
asks: Can I use color to identify metals?
What causes the color in a flame test?

faq.q: Do I need to heat the sample for gas tests?
faq.a: Sometimes heating is needed to release the gas, but some tests involve passing the gas through a liquid solution directly. Always follow the specific procedure.
asks: Is heat always necessary for gas tests?
How do I prepare a gas sample for testing?

faq.q: What does 'acidified' mean in the context of testing?
faq.a: It means that a small amount of acid, like dilute hydrochloric acid, is added to the test solution. This helps to keep the test reaction going correctly.
asks: Why do I need acid for some tests?
What is the purpose of acid in chemical tests?

faq.q: Can I test for more than one ion at the same time?
faq.a: It is best to test for ions one at a time. This keeps your results clear and prevents colors from mixing and confusing your identification.
asks: Are my results reliable if I mix samples?

facts: Sodium ions typically produce a bright yellow flame color.
A precipitate is an insoluble solid formed during a chemical reaction in solution.
Flame tests rely on the excitation energy of metal atoms.
Gas tests often involve observing a change in color or the formation of a gas.

quiz.say: If a solution turns blue when tested with potassium permanganate, what gas might be present?
quiz.why: Chlorine gas is known to cause a distinct blue color change when tested this way.

wrong.0: Ammonia gas usually causes a different color change or reaction.
wrong.1: Oxygen gas typically does not cause a strong visible color change in this specific test.
wrong.2: Hydrogen gas is usually tested by its reaction with potassium permanganate, not by a blue color.

quiz.say: When mixing silver nitrate and sodium chloride, what is the expected result?
quiz.why: Silver chloride is insoluble in water, so it forms a solid precipitate.

wrong.0: This suggests no reaction occurred, but a precipitate is expected.
wrong.1: The ions involved do not form a blue solid precipitate.
wrong.2: The reaction between these two salts primarily forms a solid, not a gas.

quiz.say: Which metal ion is most likely to produce a lilac flame?
quiz.why: Potassium ions are characteristically associated with a lilac or pale purple flame color.

wrong.0: Calcium typically produces an orange-red or brick-red color.
wrong.1: Copper ions are known for producing a distinct blue-green color.
wrong.3: Sodium always gives a very intense, bright yellow color.
